fluff.overview: The Bokkusu is the logistics element of the Teppō combined arms system, a purpose-built seventy-five ton cargo and repair trailer designed to provide field maintenance and resupply capability for the Teppō artillery vehicle and attached formations. Developed alongside the Teppō and Tenmaku by Pesht Motors and assembled at the Unity facility, the Bokkusu reflects the DCMS's recognition that sustained combat effectiveness requires reliable forward support infrastructure. By towing a fully equipped repair platform directly with the artillery vehicle, the Teppō system achieves a degree of operational self-sufficiency uncommon in heavy support platforms, reducing dependence on rearward logistics chains during extended operations.
fluff.capabilities:
The Bokkusu is a purposefully straightforward cargo and repair platform, prioritizing internal volume and structural reliability over sophisticated weaponry or sensors. Its interior accommodates tools, spare components, and consumable supplies sufficient to support the Teppō during sustained field operations. This forward repair capability allows the Teppō system to address battle damage and mechanical wear without returning to a fixed support base, extending the combined arms package's effective operational range significantly.

The trailer's systems are kept deliberately simple to maximize available cargo capacity and minimize maintenance complexity in the field. Defensive systems are minimal compared to the Tenmaku, consistent with the Bokkusu's role as a logistics asset rather than a command node. Like the Tenmaku, the Bokkusu lacks independent mobility and relies entirely on the Teppō for repositioning. Both trailers are engineered to be towed simultaneously, allowing the Teppō to move the complete combined arms package as a single tactical unit.
fluff.deployment: The Bokkusu is deployed exclusively as part of the Teppō combined arms system, towed alongside the Tenmaku command trailer during both strategic transport and field operations. It is not designed for independent operation or reassignment to other units. The first Bokkusu trailers were deployed to the Ryuken-san along with the initial Teppō systems. Broader distribution was planned contingent on the Teppō system's field evaluation results, with each assigned Teppō expected to receive both trailers as standard equipment.
fluff.history:
The Bokkusu was developed as the logistics complement to the Teppō system under the same DCMS development contract, addressing a practical dimension of the Ryuken regiments' operational review. The Ryuken's survival advantage during the Jihad stemmed not only from combined arms doctrine but from strong organic logistics practices that kept their vehicles functional longer than comparably engaged units. Without dedicated forward maintenance capability, even the most capable artillery system would eventually be reduced to inactivity by cumulative battle damage and mechanical attrition in sustained operations.

Pesht Motors designed the Bokkusu to translate this logistics discipline into dedicated hardware, providing a repair and resupply capability that travels with the artillery platform rather than remaining at a distant base. Initial deployment accompanied the Teppō to the Ryuken-san, placing the logistics trailer with the same formation whose history had shaped the entire system's doctrine. The Bokkusu was expected to accompany every Teppō assigned to DCMS formations, with its distribution planned to follow the same allocation model as the artillery vehicle and Tenmaku command trailer.
